ca_joe_brown.blurb: A small cliff on the hillside of Mt. Rubidoux above Riverside, in the Inland Empire. Almost everything here is top-rope, with a single boulder problem, and the routes run from easy fifth class near 5.6 up through the 5.11 range, with the harder end holding the most lines. The face points northwest, so it keeps shade through the morning in summer and takes the sun on cooler winter days. Anchors are simple to build from existing bolts, posts, a tree and cracks, but bring your own slings and cord. Quick to reach from town and handy for a short session.

ca_grinch_boulder_the.blurb: A roadside boulder in Christmas Valley, in the Meyers area on the south side of Lake Tahoe. It holds ten problems, running from a very easy start up to a hard V7, with the bulk of them in the V1 to V4 range. Several make good warm-ups, with pleasant top-outs and a walk-off or downclimb, though the grades can feel soft or the lines may be done differently than intended. The boulder can be seen from the road and is a minute or so from the pullouts, so it fits well alongside the other Christmas Valley blocks nearby.

ca_glass_pyramid_the.blurb: A pyramid-shaped boulder on the east side of the Camp 4 boulders in Yosemite Valley, a short walk into the trees from the campground. Ten problems cover the lower end of the scale well: a couple of very easy lines, a handful of V0 to V2 faces, arete and traverse problems, and a few harder sit starts and slabs topping out around V4. Smeary, polished-feeling friction climbing is the theme, which suits warming up or introducing newer boulderers before heading to the steeper classics of the neighbourhood.

ca_max_boulder_the.blurb: A single shaded boulder right beside Highway 20 in the Bowman and Emeralds district of the I-80 corridor near Lake Tahoe, at roughly 5,300 feet. It carries ten problems with a wide spread: several easy V0 lines, a couple of mid-grade V4 problems, and a stack of serious testpieces from V7 up to V9. The boulder is visible from the roadside pullout, so there is almost no walk, and it makes a quick stop on a trip to the nearby Emeralds sport walls rather than a full-day destination.

ca_northeast_side_2.blurb: A sport-climbing section of Fairview Dome on Fairview Mountain, near Apple Valley in the High Desert. It sits at the southern end of the Middle Earth valley, south of the slabs. Ten bolted routes run from 5.8 to 5.11, split roughly evenly between the 5.8 to 5.9 range, the 5.10s and the 5.11s, so there is something for climbers stepping up as well as those pushing harder. Most lines are rated a couple of stars or better, and it pairs naturally with the other faces on the dome.

ca_northeast_face_2.blurb: The largest face at Cragmont Park, a small city crag in the Berkeley Hills. The climbing is on a cracked slab, with a mix of short trad lines and top-rope routes from about 5.6 to the 5.10 range, most of them in the easy-to-moderate bracket. Bolted anchors on top and a tree make rigging easy, and every route can be walked off. It is widely seen as one of the best places in the East Bay to bring beginners, so expect it to be busy on nice days.
